_meta.source: Hand-curated from the sources listed per event
notes: Linked means the cited source ties the event to El Niño; coincident means it only occurred during that winter.
Coverage favors well-sourced events and is sparse for older, moderate and weak winters.

events.title: Drought cuts Indian agricultural output
events.impact: 50% agricultural losses were reported during India's 1957-58 drought.
events.note: The source documents the drought but does not attribute this event to El Niño.

source.title: Report of the FAO Asia-Pacific Conference

events.title: Failed monsoon and drought in India
events.impact: 20% was the approximate fall in India's foodgrain output during the drought.
events.note: The source documents the drought but does not attribute this event to El Niño.

source.title: The State of Food and Agriculture 1989

events.title: Drought cuts Southeast Asian rice crops
events.impact: 14 million tonnes of global rice production were lost in 1972 amid El Niño-driven drought and wider bad weather.
events.note: FAO says El Niño caused the regional drought; the production loss is global.

source.title: The Rice Crisis: Markets, Policies and Food Security

events.title: Peruvian anchoveta fishery collapse
events.impact: 11.2 million tonnes were caught in 1971 before the 1972-73 stock collapse.
events.note: FAO identifies both heavy fishing and El Niño as primary causes.

source.title: Review of the state of world marine fishery resources

events.title: Drought across southeastern Australia
events.impact: 31% of crop and livestock output was lost; sheep numbers fell by 6 million and cattle by almost 2 million.
events.note: The source documents the drought but does not attribute this event to El Niño.

source.title: Report of the FAO Asia-Pacific Conference

events.title: Long drought across Indonesia
events.impact: 11 months of drought ran from April 1982 to April 1983, with rain reported only in December.

source.title: Report on Public Policies Affecting Forest Fires

events.title: Floods in coastal Peru and Ecuador
events.impact: 298,000 people were left homeless by floods in the affected Andean countries.
events.note: The figure covers floods in Bolivia, Ecuador and Peru.

source.title: Natural disasters and their economic and social impact

events.title: Ash Wednesday bushfires
events.impact: 75 people died, 1,500 were injured and 2,000 homes were destroyed in Victoria and South Australia.
events.note: The source cites a 10-month drought but does not attribute the fires to El Niño.

source.title: Ash Wednesday Bushfire, 1983

events.title: Drought in southern Africa
events.impact: Severe drought affected southern Africa during the global weather disruption.
events.note: FAO says the drought may have been linked to El Niño.

source.title: The State of Food and Agriculture 1983

events.title: Cyclones across French Polynesia
events.impact: The worst cyclones in living memory struck Polynesia during the El Niño.

source.title: The State of Food and Agriculture 1983

events.title: Mudslides in Peru
events.impact: Whole villages were buried by mudslides during the El Niño.

source.title: The State of Food and Agriculture 1983

events.title: Forest and land fires in East Kalimantan
events.impact: 3.6 million hectares burned in Indonesia during the El Niño-linked drought.

source.title: Report on Public Policies Affecting Forest Fires

events.title: Agricultural drought in Botswana
events.impact: Severe agricultural drought affected Botswana across two crop seasons.
events.note: The 1986-87 and 1987-88 El Ninos formed one uninterrupted 19-month warm period.

source.title: Understanding the drought impact of El Nino on global agricultural areas

events.title: Severe agricultural drought in India
events.impact: 6% to 10% of foodgrain output was lost, equal to 9 to 12 million tonnes.
events.note: The cited source documents the drought but does not attribute this event to El Niño.

source.title: The State of Food and Agriculture 1989

events.title: Regional drought in southern Africa
events.impact: 18 million people faced famine after cereal output nearly halved and food-aid needs reached 4 million tonnes.

source.title: The impact of El Nino and weather anomalies on Southern African crops

events.title: Drought in Botswana and Zimbabwe
events.impact: Strong agricultural drought affected Botswana and Zimbabwe in the first crop season.

source.title: Understanding the drought impact of El Nino on global agricultural areas

events.title: Forest and peat fires across Indonesia
events.impact: 10 million hectares burned and 20 million people were exposed to haze across Southeast Asia.
events.note: The source says human ignition was the main cause; El Niño drought spread the fires.

source.title: Indonesia Environment Monitor 2003

events.title: Drought cuts Indonesian paddy production
events.impact: 2 million tonnes less paddy was produced than in 1996, mainly from late-1997 drought damage.

source.title: Drought-reduced harvest threatens food security in Indonesia

events.title: Juba and Shebelle river floods
events.impact: 2,000 people died and 250,000 were displaced by Somalia's floods.

source.title: Heavy rains attributed to El Nino cause crop damage in Eastern Africa

events.title: Drought and frost in Papua New Guinea
events.impact: 1 million people suffered food insecurity during the 1997-98 drought.

source.title: 2015-2016 El Nino: early action and response report

events.title: Coastal floods in northern Peru and Ecuador
events.impact: Significant flooding and mudslides struck western Ecuador and northwestern Peru.

source.title: Climate Assessment for 1998

events.title: Winter flooding across California
events.impact: El Niño-related rainfall caused flooding across California and much of the central and southern United States.

source.title: Climate Assessment for 1998

events.title: Drought across the Philippines
events.impact: 2.6 million people were affected by drought in 1998.

source.title: 2015-2016 El Nino: early action and response report

events.title: Widespread drought across Australia
events.impact: 61% of Australia had rainfall below the 10th percentile from March to December 2002.

source.title: Annual Climate Report 2002

events.title: Agricultural drought in East Africa
events.impact: Severe agricultural drought affected Somalia, coastal Kenya and Uganda.

source.title: Understanding the drought impact of El Nino on global agricultural areas

events.title: Drought in southern and coastal Australia
events.impact: 8 dry months put large parts of southern and coastal Australia in the lowest 10% of rainfall.

source.title: Australian rainfall during El Nino and La Nina events

events.title: Agricultural drought in Kenya
events.impact: 30 years had passed since Kenya's agricultural areas experienced a drought this severe.

source.title: Understanding the drought impact of El Nino on global agricultural areas

events.title: Poor monsoon cuts India's rice crop
events.impact: India's main-season rice crop was forecast lower after the poor summer monsoon.
events.note: FAO said some analysts also associated the poor monsoon with El Niño.

source.title: Crop Prospects and Food Situation, November 2009

events.title: Forest and peat fires across Indonesia
events.impact: 2.6 million hectares burned and the fires cost Indonesia an estimated US$16.1 billion.
events.note: The fires were human-set; drought and El Niño worsened their spread.

source.title: The Cost of Fire: An Economic Analysis of Indonesia's 2015 Fire Crisis

events.title: Drought and crop failure in Ethiopia
events.impact: 10.2 million people were driven into food insecurity after repeated crop failure and livestock losses.

source.title: FAO presents $50 million emergency plan as Ethiopia faces worst drought in 30 years

events.title: Drought and frost in Papua New Guinea
events.impact: 2.7 million people were affected by drought, frost and forest fires.

source.title: 2015-2016 El Nino: early action and response report

events.title: Drought across southern Africa
events.impact: 26% drop was forecast for the 2016 regional cereal harvest from the already reduced 2015 level.

source.title: Ongoing conflicts and droughts exacerbate food needs

events.title: Drought in Central America's Dry Corridor
events.impact: 3.5 million people needed humanitarian assistance, including 1.6 million who were food insecure.
events.note: The drought compounded dry conditions from the prior year.

source.title: To reduce El Nino's impact on Central America's Dry Corridor

events.title: Mekong Delta drought and saltwater intrusion
events.impact: 2 million people had limited water access and 820,000 hectares of crops were affected.

source.title: Agricultural Land Use and Sustainable Livelihoods in the Mekong Delta

events.title: Great Barrier Reef mass bleaching
events.impact: 29% of shallow-water coral cover was lost after the 2016 bleaching event.
events.note: The source cites high sea temperatures combined with strong El Niño.

source.title: Experimental Environmental-Economic Accounts for the Great Barrier Reef, 2017

events.title: Black Summer bushfires in eastern Australia
events.impact: 5 million hectares had burned, 18 people had died and more than 1,600 homes were destroyed by 31 December.
events.note: ENSO was neutral; a strong positive Indian Ocean Dipole was a main climate influence.

source.title: Annual climate statement 2019

events.title: Record-low rivers in the Brazilian Amazon
events.impact: 120+ years of observations were broken when the Negro River at Manaus fell to a record low.
events.note: WMO cites El Niño alongside long-term climate change.

source.title: El Nino and climate change impacts slam Latin America and Caribbean in 2023

events.title: Floods across the Greater Horn of Africa
events.impact: 352 people died and 2.4 million were displaced across Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya.
events.note: WMO attributes the heavy rains to both El Niño and the positive Indian Ocean Dipole.

source.title: Supplement to the State of the Global Climate 2023

events.title: Panama Canal drought restrictions
events.impact: 41% less rain than normal fell in October, prompting planned reservation cuts to 18 daily slots by February.

source.title: El mes de octubre mas seco desde 1950

events.title: Drought cuts southern African harvests
events.impact: 43% and 50% below average were Zambia's and Zimbabwe's 2024 cereal harvests, respectively.
events.note: Percentages are against the 2019-2023 five-year average.

source.title: State of the Climate in Africa 2024

events.title: Extreme heat across Southeast Asia
events.impact: 30 heat-related deaths were recorded in Thailand by 24 April, with schools and work disrupted across the region.
events.note: WMO cites El Niño and climate change as drivers of the high temperatures.

source.title: Widespread parts of Asia and Africa reel under extreme weather

events.title: Floods across Rio Grande do Sul
events.impact: 2.4 million people were affected across 478 municipalities and 183 people died.
events.note: ANA also cites climate change and failures in flood-protection systems.

source.title: Estudo aponta que enchentes de 2024 foram maior desastre natural da historia do RS
